question: Why does an inner function still have access to outer variables after the outer function returns?
options: The variables are copied onto the global window object
The JavaScript engine preserves the lexical environment record as long as a reference to the inner function exists
Functions re-execute the outer function each time they are called
Closures run in a separate Web Worker thread
explanation: Functions hold a hidden reference to their enclosing lexical scope. The garbage collector does not destroy the environment while live references exist.
